rejected.title: Mnemonics
card: A mnemonic is a memory aid. It links new information to a cue that is easier to recall, so the cue can bring the information back.
Acronym
a word made from the first letters of items to remember. ROY G BIV stands for the colours of the rainbow.
Acrostic
a sentence where the first letter of each word stands for an item. The words are chosen to make a phrase that is easy to recall.
Method of loci
the student pictures a familiar route or place and puts each item at a stop along it. To recall the items, they walk through the route in their mind.
rejected.remember: A mnemonic ties new information to an easier cue, such as a word, a sentence or a place.

a.q: Which of these is an example of the method of loci?
opts: Placing each item to learn at a stop on a route through home
Making a word from the first letters of the items to learn
Writing a sentence whose words start with each item's letter
Repeating the list aloud many times until it is familiar
a.why: The method of loci uses a familiar place as the cue, with one item at each stop. Making a word from first letters is an acronym, and a sentence of first letters is an acrostic. Repeating a list does not link the items to any cue, so it is not a mnemonic.
a.clue: Which options rely on first letters, and which one links items to a cue?

b.q: Priya must learn the order of the planets. She remembers the sentence 'My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Naming', where each word starts with the first letter of a planet, in order. Which mnemonic is this, and what is the cue?
opts: An acrostic, and the cue is the sentence
An acronym, and the cue is the sentence
An acrostic, and the cue is a familiar place
An acronym, and the cue is a single made-up word
b.why: The first letters are used to build a whole sentence, so this is an acrostic. The sentence is the cue that brings back each planet's first letter. An acronym would be a single word made from the letters, not a sentence.
b.clue: Is the memory aid a single word or a full sentence?
